questions.question: Which is the layer of epidermis present in thick skin and comment on it? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Which is the layer of epidermis present in thick skin and comment on it? [U]/[CO3] ● The layer of epidermis present only in thick skin is the Stratum lucidum. ● It is a thin, clear, transparent layer found between the stratum granulosum and stratum corneum. ● Present only in palms of the hands and soles of the feet. ● Made up of dead, flattened keratinocytes containing eleidin, a translucent protein that helps protect underlying layers. ● Provides extra protection and reduces friction in areas exposed to constant pressure. (Stratum lucidum- 1 mark, any one comment- 1 mark)

questions.question: Give the pathway of visual impulses from the retina to the visual cortex. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Give the pathway of visual impulses from the retina to the visual cortex. [U]/[CO3] ● Retina (Rods & Cones) → Bipolar Cells → Ganglion Cells → Optic Nerve → Optic Chiasma → Optic Tract → Lateral Geniculate Body (Thalamus) → Optic Radiations → Visual Cortex (Occipital Lobe). ( NB : A clear, precise flowchart showing the sequence is sufficient for full marks; no diagram or detailed explanation is needed.)

questions.question: Describe the function of the middle ear. / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Describe the function of the middle ear. [U]/[CO1,CO2] ● Transmission of sound: Transfers sound vibrations from the tympanic membrane (eardrum) to the inner ear through the ossicles — malleus, incus, and stapes. ● Amplification: The ossicles amplify the sound vibrations to overcome the resistance of the fluid in the inner ear. ● Pressure equalization: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and helps equalize air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. ● Protection: The tensor tympani and stapedius muscles protect the inner ear from loud sounds by dampening excessive vibrations. (Any 2 points: 1 mark each)

questions.solution_html: • Mention the ordered sequence of auditory relay stations from periphery to cortex. questions.question: A woman with PCOD complains of infertility. How do assisted reproductive techniques apply in her management? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • A woman with PCOD complains of infertility. How do assisted reproductive techniques apply in her management? [A]/[CO4] ● Ovulation induction therapy – Use of drugs like Clomiphene citrate , Letrozole , or Gonadotropins to stimulate ovulation. ● Intrauterine insemination (IUI) – Washed sperm are directly introduced into the uterus near the time of ovulation. ● In vitro fertilization (IVF) – Eggs are collected, fertilized in the lab, and the resulting embryos are transferred to the uterus. ● Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) – A single sperm is injected directly into an egg; used when sperm count or motility is low. ● Laparoscopic ovarian drilling (LOD) – A surgical technique to destroy androgen-producing tissue, improving ovulation. ● Cryopreservation of embryos or oocytes – Useful for preserving fertility if repeated cycles are needed. ● Lifestyle modification support – Though not ART itself, weight reduction and insulin-sensitizing drugs like metformin enhance ART success. (Any two methods with explanations or four methods mentioned briefly can be given full marks.)

questions.question: Write short notes on Graves’ disease. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • Write short notes on Graves’ disease. [U]/[CO4] ● Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hyperthyroidism. ● The body produces TSH receptor antibodies that overstimulate the thyroid gland. ● Leads to excess secretion of thyroid hormones (T ₃ and T ₄ ). ● Symptoms: weight loss, heat intolerance, rapid heartbeat, tremors, anxiety, and exophthalmos (bulging eyes). ● Treatment: antithyroid drugs, radioactive iodine therapy, or partial thyroidectomy. (Liberal valuation)

[K]/[CO4] ● Lithium – the most common and effective traditional mood stabilizer ● Valproate (Valproic acid) – controls manic episodes ● Carbamazepine – used when lithium is not tolerated ● Lamotrigine – effective for preventing depressive episodes ● Atypical antipsychotics – such as olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone for mood stabilization ● Psychotherapy – cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) helps manage mood swings ● Mindfulness and meditation – reduce stress and emotional instability ● Regular sleep schedule – stabilizes mood and prevents manic/depressive triggers ● Physical exercise – boosts endorphins and supports emotional balance ● Avoidance of alcohol and recreational drugs – prevents worsening of symptoms ● Support groups and family therapy – improve emotional regulation and adherence to treatment. (Any one stabilizer

questions.question: Describe the functional importance of olfaction in daily life activities. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the functional importance of olfaction in daily life activities. [U]/[CO1] ● Detection of hazards: Helps identify dangers such as smoke, gas leaks, or spoiled food. ● Enhancement of taste: Works with taste buds to create the perception of flavor. ● Emotional connection: Certain smells evoke memories and emotions. ● Social communication: Body odor and perfumes influence social interactions and attraction. ● Appetite regulation: Pleasant food odors stimulate appetite, while unpleasant ones suppress it. ● Environmental awareness: Helps recognize surroundings and personal hygiene. (Explanation of any 4 points- 4 marks or a good account on functional importance

questions.question: Explain the different primary taste sensations and give examples. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Explain the different primary taste sensations and give examples. [U]/[CO2] ● Sweet: Caused by sugars and some amino acids — e.g., candy, honey, fruits. ● Sour: Produced by acids — e.g., lemon, vinegar. ● Salty: Due to salts, mainly sodium ions — e.g., table salt, chips. ● Bitter: Often from alkaloids — e.g., coffee, cocoa, neem. ● Umami: A savory taste from glutamate and certain amino acids — e.g., meat, cheese, soy sauce. (Mentioning all five primary tastes and example :2 mark, Brief explanation:2 marks)

questions.question: Explain how nociceptors are involved in the perception of pain through the skin. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Explain how nociceptors are involved in the perception of pain through the skin. [U]/[CO3] ● Nociceptors are specialized sensory receptors in the skin that detect painful or damaging stimuli such as extreme heat, pressure, or chemicals. ● When activated, they generate nerve impulses that travel through sensory neurons to the spinal cord. ● These impulses are then relayed to the brain, particularly the thalamus and somatosensory cortex, where pain is perceived. ● This mechanism helps the body recognize and respond to potential harm, promoting protective actions like withdrawal from the source of injury. (definition:1 mark, Comment: 3 marks or a good account on nociceptors: 4 marks)

questions.question: Describe the important functions of endocrine system in our body. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • Describe the important functions of the endocrine system in our body. [U]/[CO4] ● Regulates metabolism: Controls energy production and nutrient use through hormones like insulin and thyroxine. ● Maintains homeostasis: Keeps internal conditions stable, including blood pressure, temperature, and water balance. ● Controls growth and development: Growth hormone and thyroid hormones promote body growth and tissue development. ● Regulates reproduction: Hormones like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone control sexual development and fertility. ● Coordinates stress response: Adrenal hormones such as cortisol and adrenaline help the body respond to stress. ● Regulates mood and behavior: Hormones influence emotions, sleep, and mental well-being. ● Regulates blood glucose levels: Insulin and glucagon maintain normal blood sugar balance. ● Controls calcium and bone metabolism: Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin regulate calcium levels and bone strength. ● Influences circadian rhythm: Melatonin from the pineal gland controls sleep–wake cycles. ● Aids in digestion: Hormones like gastrin, secretin, and cholecystokinin regulate digestive processes. ● Supports immune function: Thymosin promotes immune cell development. ● Regulates blood pressure and fluid balance: Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone (ADH) maintain water and salt balance. ● Promotes cell repair and regeneration: Growth factors assist in tissue maintenance and healing. ● Integrates with the nervous system: Works with the hypothalamus to coordinate body responses to internal and external changes . (Explain any 4 points with brief explanations – 4 marks or mention any correct 6 points- 4 marks)

questions.question: Explain the interaction between sympathetic nervous system and adrenal medulla in stress. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • Explain the interaction between the sympathetic nervous system and adrenal medulla in stress. [U]/[CO4] ● During stress, the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is activated as part of the “fight or flight” response. ● The SNS stimulates the adrenal medulla (inner part of the adrenal gland) through sympathetic nerve fibers. ● The adrenal medulla then releases epinephrine (adrenaline) and norepinephrine (noradrenaline) into the bloodstream. ● These hormones increase heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, and glucose release, preparing the body to handle stress. ● This shows a close coordination where the SNS provides rapid nerve stimulation, and the adrenal medulla ensures a prolonged hormonal effect to manage stress efficiently. (Give full marks for relevant explanation)

questions.question: Discuss how hormonal changes in the ovaries prepare the female body for fertilization and implantation. / [CO4] [4x5 = 20]
questions.solution_html: • Discuss how hormonal changes in the ovaries prepare the female body for fertilization and implantation. [U]/[CO4] ● Follicular phase: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) promotes the growth of ovarian follicles, which secrete estrogen. Estrogen thickens the endometrium and prepares the cervix for sperm entry. ● Ovulation: A surge in luteinizing hormone (LH) triggers the release of an egg (ovum) from the ovary. ● Luteal phase: After ovulation, the corpus luteum forms and secretes progesterone and some estrogen. ● Progesterone stabilizes and further thickens the endometrium, making it suitable for implantation. ● If fertilization occurs, progesterone continues to support the uterine lining; if not, hormone levels drop, leading to menstruation. ( 1 mark each for mentioning each phase (follicular, ovulation, luteal, and outcome) along with the specific hormone involved and its function.)
